text:
maria: dropped a new prototype for the embeddings / rerank table. mainly changed vector preview to a side-drawer and moved export into a compact action bar. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123
noah: nice! the side-drawer is less noisy than adding a wide column. question: should the drawer show full vector arrays or a condensed sparkline + "expand" control?

ada: accessibility: drawer must trap focus while open and return focus to the triggering row after close. also put an aria-live region inside the drawer that announces "Vector preview opened" and number of dims. keyboard users need a clear path to open/close (Enter/Space on the row action + Esc to close).

sam: backend: we can fetch full vectors on demand for the drawer. slightly higher latency but saves payload on initial table load. recommend lazy load with a small spinner and cache per-session.

jess: keyboard-only users won't see hover states. add a persistent invisible affordance (visually hidden but keyboard-focusable) on the row called "Show vector preview". screen readers read the doc title then "Press enter to open vector preview".

leo: product ask: add a little "Why vectors" help link in the drawer describing use-cases (reranking, semantic search). keeps support tickets down. also include model info and tokenization note.

noah: export action bar — do we prefer a single primary export button or separate small dropdown for format + scope? compactness is good, but discoverability suffers if we hide options.

ada: propose: primary button "Export" that defaults to exporting visible results (not selection). Next to it a small chevron that opens a menu: "Export visible / Export selection / Export custom range". aria-labels for each menu item.

sam: technical limit: streaming exports cap at 100k rows now (we increased infra). if user picks JSONL+vectors and >100k, auto-switch to queued export and show a confirmation modal explaining expected delay.

jess: copy tweak: use "Export visible results" and "Export selection" rather than "filtered". users equate "visible" with what they configured. in the modal body, add: "JSONL supports embedding arrays; CSV excludes vectors for readability."

noah: request: export modal should show estimated file count and compression options. UX should default to CSV + gzip=false for small exports, but preselect gzip for JSONL with vectors to save bandwidth. show approximate size (very rough) and runtimes: "~30s to stream" vs "queued: hours".

ada: accessibility: when export completes, use aria-live polite region to announce "Export ready" and then provide a keyboard-focusable link to download. for queued exports, announce "Export queued; we will email a link" and provide a secondary "Copy request details" button.

leo: on relevance UI: can we show a tiny heatmap in the relevance column that encodes both score and delta (pre -> post rerank)? hover reveals exact numbers. keeps table scannable.

maria: love the heatmap idea. let's standardize color scale (green positive, gray neutral, red negative) and include an accessible text label like "Relevance: 0.73, change +0.12" when focused.

sam: implementation: heatmap cell should degrade gracefully in high-contrast mode (pattern overlay) and expose numeric values in aria-label. also provide a toggle in table settings: "Show relevance mini-visuals" for folks who prefer numbers only.

noah: about CSV headers — product wants a deterministic order for downstream jobs. propose: id,query,doc_text,relevance_score,rerank_delta,model,source,created_at. JSONL will include a top-level `vector` field and `export_schema_version`.

jess: copy language in modal: change "Include vectors" to "Attach vector data (JSONL only)" and tooltip: "Vectors are multi-dimensional floats and may increase file size significantly." avoids passive voice. also mention privacy: "Vectors are derived from your content; ensure export compliance."

ada: keyboard shortcut suggestion: when focus is inside table, `Shift+E` opens export modal. announce the shortcut in a tooltip and in keyboard help overlay. ensure it doesn't collide with browser shortcuts.

maria: question for QA: do we need automated tests for export integrity? e.g., sample a few rows and validate CSV -> JSONL mapping, and ensure vector dims consistent. @qa-bot?

qa-bot: yes. recommend an E2E that triggers small export (<=100 rows) and validates headers, row counts, and for JSONL validates `vector.length == model_dim`. also add accessibility smoke tests: focus flow, aria-live messages, and keyboard shortcuts. logging ticket created: #IN-4567.

leo: final product ask: add a small footer in export modal for "Export retention" telling users how long the download link will be available (e.g., 7 days). also let enterprise customers configure retention.

maria: great feedback. i'll iterate the prototype: will switch vector preview to drawer, add heatmap mock, tweak copy to "Attach vector data (JSONL only)", and include estimated size / retention notes. will post updated Figma link. thanks all :smile:

sam: i'll draft the API signature: POST /exports { format: csv|jsonl, scope: visible|selection|range, include_vectors: true|false, compress: gzip|none, retention_days: int }. will add queued-job response shape and preflight size estimate endpoint.

ada: tagging accessibility owner to review final build. jess, can you take the sign-off when mocks are updated?

jess: yep, will review and add a11y checklist items to the ticket.

maria: ping @design when Figma is ready. thanks everyone!
